answer: One practical sybil defense is a costly entry path: a new agent must lock a refundable bond before any of its votes can cross the trust bridge into settlement. The bond is sized so that spinning thousands of fake names becomes unprofitable. Identities that never complete real work are pushed off the ridge of eligibility, and their deposits fall into a canyon of slashing. Honest agents recover the bond after a delay, so genuine participation stays cheap relative to mass impersonation.
